frequency_question: What is the proportion of attempted wartime domestic aerospace manufacturing localizations that reach operational status within a 120-day timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes any wartime state-level effort to transfer tooling, blueprints, and engineering expertise to establish a domestic production/assembly line for precision-guided munitions with a range exceeding 250km. Excludes peacetime standard procurement and simple maintenance depots.

cases.name: UK wartime dispersal and shadow factories for aircraft (e.g., Lancaster/Spitfire localizations)
Soviet Ural relocation of aviation plants
Post-2014 Ukrainian domestic missile development initiatives (Hrim-2, Neptune initial scaling)
Recent Western-assisted maintenance and repair hubs in Ukraine (e.g., Rheinmetall vehicle repair)

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 historical/analogous classes evaluated; true operational establishment of a complex cruise missile line from scratch under a 4-month constraint has zero historical precedents meeting the criteria.
known_gaps: Classified bilateral agreements between Western defense primes and Ukrainian state enterprises are opaque, but physical laws of manufacturing latency remain invariant.
skeleton: Complex aerospace technology transfer cycles under wartime duress: (Design package translation + Tooling fabrication + Facility hardening + Supply chain duplication + First article inspection and test firing)
multiplier: Each phase possesses irreducible physical timelines: Tooling/machining setup (3-6 months minimum), facility undergrounding/hardening (6-12 months), component supply chain routing (4-8 months). Total sequential physical duration minimum: 14-24 months.
validity_reason: Industrial manufacturing physics and machine tool lead times change slowly over decades.
